legend: Duodenal biopsy demonstrates marked infiltration of the lamina propria by a dense lymphoid infiltrate with splaying of crypts and overlying villous blunting (<<30624>>). Details are shown at higher magnification (<<30625>>). High-power examination shows that the infiltrate consists of small cells with round, eccentric nuclei and moderate pink cytoplasm, histologically consistent with an extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (EMZL) with extensive plasmacytic differentiation (<<30626>>). Immunohistochemical stains (not shown) demonstrated that the plasmacytic cells were positive for alpha heavy chain, with little to no staining for mu and gamma heavy chains or kappa and lambda light chains, supporting a diagnosis of alpha heavy chain disease or immunoproliferative small intestinal disease.

Lymph node biopsy showing complete architectural effacement by a diffuse, polymorphous infiltrate of small lymphocytes, plasmacytoid lymphocytes, plasma cells, and immunoblasts with prominent nucleoli (<<30631>>). Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma arising in the setting of alpha heavy chain disease: areas of the lymph node contain more monomorphic collections of large immunoblasts with prominent nucleoli and clumped chromatin, some of which have eccentric cytoplasm and paranuclear hof suggestive of plasmablastic differentiation (<<30632>>). The Ki-67 proliferation index (not shown) was approximately 80% in these areas and the overall findings were consistent with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with immunoblastic/plasmablastic differentiation. Most of the large cells are positive for IRF4 (MUM1) (<<30633>>), with diffuse staining for alpha heavy chain (<<30634>>), but are negative for both kappa (<<30635>>) and lambda light chains, which are positive in a few scattered polytypic plasma cells (<<30636>>).

Duodenal biopsy demonstrates marked infiltration of the lamina propria by a dense lymphoid infiltrate, with splaying of crypts and overlying villous blunting. The infiltrate is composed of small cells with round, eccentric nuclei and moderate pink cytoplasm. The findings are consistent with an extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma) with extensive plasmacytic differentiation (H&E). In the context of additional immunohistochemical stains (not shown) demonstrating the plasmacytic cells to be positive for alpha heavy chain with no staining for kappa or lambda light chains, a diagnosis of alpha heavy chain disease or immunoproliferative small intestinal disease can be made.
